The identifier is a version 7 UUID: its first 48 bits are the session’s start in Unix milliseconds,
which every record’s timestamp sends anyway, and the rest is random, derived from nothing. It lives
in the enricher’s memory only, and the next launch’s tracker starts a new session with a new
identifier. A store keeps it beside each record of the session, so a record recovered after a
relaunch still carries its session, and it is deleted when the store deletes the record’s bytes
(a

Traffluent keeps no identifier that links one session to another.

abstract.text: Keep each record on disk until it is delivered, so a record the app tracked survives the process ending.
Keep a seeded fraction of the events a tracker tracks, event by event or a whole session at once.
Deliver an event only once the user grants the purpose it is collected for.
Send events to an analytics vendor Traffluent doesn’t cover yet, from a module of your own, with the same rules as the destinations it ships.
Typed analytics events for Swift, delivered in batches to any number of destinations.
Traffluent knows people only by a pseudonymous session. An identifier that outlives one is yours to add, store, reset and gate with consent.
Deliver events to your logs, your traces, a server or memory, and decide what each destination may see.
Put every event a tracker tracks in a session, and sample whole sessions.
Track screen views, control activations and the app’s lifecycle without a call at each place they happen.

abstract.text: Tell the people and services that read your events what each event holds, and hear about a change that would break their data before it ships.
Stamp every event with the app, device, operating system, locale and network connection it was tracked on.
Track the app’s installs, updates, opens, moves to the background and terminations, and make the
tracker’s records durable as the app leaves the foreground.
